# LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate
> each answer token (decode), although generation is almost all decoding. We untie the two loop counts (prefill m
> loops, decode n < m) and introduce LoopBridge (2.4% of parameters on Ouro-2.6B; 0.017-0.25% on 26.4B sparse-MoE
> looped models: cache-foldable prompt KV maps + optional decoder LoRA), a lightweight adapter distilled from the
> full-loop model that folds into the prompt cache once at prefill with virtually zero per-token decode overhead.
> Evaluated on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B, Thinking models, Lev decision models, and 26.4B sparse-MoE looped models
> (TML-d24-varloop-research and Inkling-2-Mini) in Day-0 vLLM. Every number is recomputed from released per-item scores
> by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py (Ouro) and inkling/make_figs.py (26.4B MoE).

Main findings (95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- At batch 1 on Ouro-2.6B, prefill is 0.3-2.6% of the wall time of a chain-of-thought request (0.1-0.3% on Thinking models).
- One decode loop (Ouro-2.6B): LoopBridge 4/1 raises the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 (Original 1/1) to 58.2
  (58.3 +- 0.1 over three seeds), above tied-loop distillation on the same data (49.5; rank 80: 49.3); at two decode
  loops, 63.7 -> 69.1 (vs 66.2 Distilled 2/2); MATH-500 zero-shot.
- Measured time (Ouro-2.6B, 800 requests, batch 1): LoopBridge 4/1 scores 45.0% (+17.2 over Original 1/1, +10.8 over
  Distilled 1/1) at 27.7 tokens/s (vs 28.3 for Original 1/1) and +10.5 points over a time-matched Original 1/1-2/2 mix;
  4/2 runs at 14.3 tokens/s (2.1x Original 4/4). At batch 32, LoopBridge 4/1 stays +18.5 / +11.3 points ahead in
  1.18x / 1.19x time.
- The gain peaks within two to five prefill loops (also for an adapter trained to 16 loops, over seeds, and with the
  prefill loops trained too).
- Transfers to Ouro-1.4B (44.5 at 4/1, 44.2 +- 0.2 over three seeds, vs 40.5 distilled and 34.7 original),
  Ouro-2.6B-Thinking (4/2 within 0.8 points of 4/4 on average and +3.1 above Distilled 2/2; served in batches, matches
  Original 4/4 on all 1,319 GSM8K problems at 2.0x throughput and 0.47-0.57x wall time), and Lev decision models.
- Scales 10x to 26.4B sparse-MoE looped models in Day-0 vLLM (TML-d24-varloop-research & Inkling-2-Mini) on five
  official reasoning and 256K-1M benchmarks (GPQA Diamond, LiveCodeBench v6, MRCR v2 8n 256K-512K, GraphWalks BFS 256K,
  LongBench v2 1M), establishing a two-regime law:
  * Regime I (variable-depth TML-d24-varloop at n >= 2, 19 arms, full 5x avg@4 = 81,776 rollouts):
    training-free untying works natively (4/2: 68.4-68.9 vs 66.9 Orig 2/2; 4/3: 73.3-74.0 vs 73.1 Orig 3/3), and
    pure-prompt KV-Only maps (lora_rank=0, 4.46M-6.55M params = 17-25 MiB = 0.017-0.025%, 0% decode overhead) lead both
    dedicated depths: LB 4/2 KV-Only reaches 69.6% (+2.78 [+0.82, +4.67] 5-Bench, +4.29 [+1.37, +7.18]
    3-Long, +9.54 [+2.91, +16.49] MRCR 512K over Orig 2/2, all surviving k=3 Holm-Bonferroni 98.33% CIs, plus +1.99
    [+0.25, +3.73] 95% CI on uncloned 1M LongBench v2 [+3.34 [+0.98, +5.78] p=0.0052 on strictly 13-gram-clean N=307
    vs -0.13 on 196 overlapped items], at 1.75x decode vs 4/4). Matched controls on identical 12M v5_onpolicy_t4 data and
    t=4 teacher isolate both untying and r=0 sufficiency: (a) tied KV-Only 2/2 (m=2, 2.36M active) is flat at 67.0% (+0.13),
    so untying m=2->4 causes +2.65 [+1.14, +4.16] 5-Bench (p<1e-3; +3.43 3-Long, +5.49 MRCR), and 0%-nosynth LB 4/2 (68.7%)
    still beats full-synthetic KV-Only 2/2 by +1.71 [+0.05, +3.35]; (b) scaling tied 2/2 to full r=64 LoRA (Distilled 2/2,
    46.9M, 5.8h) reaches only 68.9% (+2.02* vs 2/2, merely tying zero-shot TF Tail 68.9%, p=0.98), whereas exact-twin r=64
    LB 4/2 (40.6M, 2.13h, 2.73x faster) reaches 69.6% (directional +0.72 [-0.90, +2.36] 5-Bench p=0.38, +4.38 MRCR,
    significant +2.63 [+0.75, +4.52] 1M LBv2 p=0.0088) and ties 9.1x-smaller r=0 LB 4/2 KV-Only (-0.03, p=0.98);
    (c) one single 11.01M (0.042%, 42.0 MiB fp32) 0%-synthetic universal adapter
    (18M tokens = 6M/cell) serves 4/3 (73.8%, 98.6% of 4/4), 3/2 (69.8%, #1 overall at n=2, +2.93 [+1.39, +4.46] p=0.0004
    and +4.64 [+2.43, +6.91] 3-Long p<1e-4 vs 2/2, +2.34 [+0.60, +4.13] LBv2 p=0.0072 vs Distilled 2/2, 25% cheaper prefill), and 4/2 (68.4%, sweeps 2/2 5/5) without reloading;
    (d) in a 3-way closed-form Plato's Key test (192 unlabeled prompts), orthogonal 1->1 Procrustes 4/2 (68.4%, 41.9%
    dark-memory CV) beats unconstrained Cross-Ridge 4/2 (60.7%, -7.63*), yet behavioral KL LB 4/2 KV-Only significantly
    beats Procrustes 4/2 on 3-Long (+2.45*) and MRCR 512K (+6.06*, 59.2% dark-memory CV). LB 4/3 KV-Only reaches 74.1%
    (99.0% of Orig 4/4's 74.9% at 1.27-1.29x decode); both beat Orig 4/4 end-to-end across all lengths up to 262K with
    9/9 step-0 & 96.8-97.9% 31-step PyTorch-vLLM parity, 1.25-3.58x moderate & saturated async Poisson ITL speedup, and
    0 preemptions under tested load matching equal-m KV occupancy.
  * Regime II (fixed-depth Inkling-2-Mini 3/2 & un-gated n=1 VarLoop 3/1, BOTH full 5x avg@4; 111,904 total four-sample
    rollouts across 26 archived 5x avg@4 arms): all unadapted n=2 variants collapse (Mini TF 3/2 Anchored: 2.2%, 93.2% trunc;
    Mini Orig 2/2 & TF 3/2 Tail: 5.6% GPQA; Mini Procrustes 3/2: 11.1% GPQA, 81.8% trunc; VarLoop TF 3/1: 40.8%), while
    parametric LoopBridge rescues accuracy and beats parameter-advantaged tied distillation under locked 24M controls on
    both backbones: Inkling-2-Mini 3/2 reaches 57.7% vs 52.0% Distilled 2/2 (+5.70 [+4.10, +7.34] 5-Bench, +9.36
    [+6.95, +11.84] 3-Long, p<1e-4, lower truncation on all 5 splits, vs 67.5% Original 3/3; 58.3% @1 at 48M v2), and
    VarLoop 3/1 sweeps Distilled 1/1 5/5 at full 5x avg@4 (50.0% vs 44.7%, +5.31 [+3.53, +7.14] 5-Bench, +8.50
    [+5.83, +11.23] 3-Long, +4.78 [+2.62, +6.95] Pure-4, p<1e-4, lower micro trunc 12.9% vs 14.5%; 3-step KV-map ladder
    climbs monotonically 48.9 -> 49.7 -> 50.0 5-Bench and 26.7 -> 29.6 -> 31.4 MRCR, with single-pass KV adding +2.37
    [+0.25, +4.48] 3-Long [p=0.030] and full cross-pass KV adding +4.70 [+0.84, +8.53] on 512K MRCR [two-sided p=0.017]).
- Baselines: the Ouro distilled baselines move by at most 0.9 points over 0.3x-3x learning rates (0.7 at rank 16, 0.9 at rank 80).

Limitations stated by the author: timing on one GPU architecture (B300) up to batch 32; on short-output 128K-256K
prompts (G=512), deeper m-pass prefill attenuates end-to-end speedup relative to shallower-m baselines (1.14-1.19x for
3/1 over 3/3 vs 2.18x pure decode; though 4/3 and 4/2 still beat equal-m Orig 4/4 end-to-end at 262K); under
unconstrained single-stream (B=1) high-effort reasoning on 26.4B models, n=1 decoders inflate chain-of-thought length
by 1.4-1.8x so n >= 2 (LoopBridge 4/3, 4/2, 3/2) dominates n=1 in single-request wall time and accuracy whereas n=1
leads in batched throughput cost; our current vLLM prototype retains m global KV slots; prefill depth is fixed per
setting rather than per prompt; English benchmarks only.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, 26.4B vLLM two-regime results, quick start, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; Ouro and 26.4B vLLM commands
- paper/loopbridge.pdf: the 36-page paper (<8-page ACL main body + Appendices A-O)
- ouro/results/items/: Ouro per-item scores; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: recomputed Ouro statistics
- inkling/results/: 26.4B sparse-MoE official-exact avg@4 & avg@1 per-item JSONs, isolated Day-0 vLLM Blackwell timing logs, and systems_rebuttal/ (parity, warmed timing, Poisson serving, KV capacity)
- ouro/results/provenance/: Ouro run manifests, logs, configs, and checkpoint hashes
- docs/ARCHIVE.md: public ModelScope checkpoints/data (`torushy/LoopBridge`, `torushy/LoopBridge-Data`) and cold-archive notes
- Checkpoints (ModelScope, 16 adapters: 8 Ouro + 8 26.4B MoE): https://modelscope.cn/models/torushy/LoopBridge
- Data (ModelScope): https://modelscope.cn/datasets/torushy/LoopBridge-Data
- docs/DEPRECATED.md: pruned legacy scripts/arms and remaining optional branches
- The tag paper-arxiv points to the exact commit the arXiv PDF and all figures/tables were built from.
